title: Public Records Request – Sheriff's Department Response to Residential Disturbance – Eastvale, CA

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request publicly disclosable written records documenting a Sheriff's Department response to a residential disturbance in Eastvale, California.

Incident Address: 13326 Rowen Court, Eastvale, CA 92880

Date Range: July 1, 2025 – November 20, 2026

Approximate Response Time: 4:00 a.m.

Known Incident Details

A concerned neighbor reportedly contacted law enforcement after hearing screaming and crying at or near the identified residence.

Responding deputies reportedly arrived at approximately 4:00 a.m. and conducted separate interviews with two adult occupants.

The exact date and incident number are currently unknown.

Records Requested

I request the following existing, publicly disclosable written records associated with this specific incident:

     1. Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) Records: Incident number, date, time, call classification, nature of the complaint, dispatcher notes, responding units and final disposition.

     2. Call-for-Service Records: Written records documenting the original complaint, dispatch activity and responding deputies' actions.

     3. Incident and Supplemental Reports: Publicly disclosable portions of incident reports, deputy narratives and supplemental reports documenting the circumstances of the response, investigative actions, observations and disposition.

     4. Incident Disposition Records: Written documentation identifying the outcome of the response, including any official actions taken by responding deputies.

Search Instructions

Because the exact incident date is unknown, please search using the property address, approximate response time and incident details provided.

Please do not restrict the search to a single incident classification, as the original complaint may have been categorized as a disturbance, noise complaint, welfare check or another call-for-service type.

This request is limited to written and electronic text-based records. No audio recordings, video recordings, photographs, body-worn camera footage or dashboard camera footage are requested.

Personally identifying information concerning private individuals, reporting parties, victims and minors may be redacted and is not requested.

Please provide reasonably segregable, nonexempt portions of responsive records. If records or information are withheld, please identify the applicable statutory exemption.

Electronic copies are preferred. Please advise of any applicable fees before processing.

Thank you for your assistance.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Chris Hoven

title: Itemized Fee Petitions, Invoices, and Settlement Payouts (McMinimee Law)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. All itemized invoices, line-item billing sheets, and fee petitions submitted to Highline Public Schools District, its legal affairs department, its board of directors, or its risk-management carriers by Shannon McMinimee or any agent operating under the domain or entity name "McMinimee Law".
2. All transactional records, ledger entries, checks, voucher approvals, board warrant registry items, or electronic funds transfer records documenting attorney fee payouts, cost reimbursements, or financial settlement distributions paid directly to McMinimee Law or Shannon McMinimee.
3. This request specifically targets but is not limited to all itemized fee breakdowns, billing blocks, and backup ledger documentation associated with any and all OSPI/OAH special education due process dockets where McMinimee Law served as counsel of record.
4. The chronological scope of this request spans from January 4, 2022, through June 30, 2025, specifically targeting all billing blocks, settlement agreements, and fee recovery actions generated while the attorney was concurrently operating under private credentials and public employment contracts.

PRE-EMPTIVE STATUTORY ENFORCEMENT & COMPLIANCE CLAUSE:
The District is advised that, per Washington law (Progressive Animal Welfare Soc. v. University of Wash.), attorney billing records for public payment are subject to disclosure. Only specific, narrow redactions (e.g., student names under FERPA) are permitted, as blanket privilege claims are invalid under Soter v. Cowles Publishing Co.

MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:
A response is expected within five business days as per RCW 42.56.520. The records, requested for non-commercial purposes, should be provided electronically.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Any and all records in the possession of the Dawson County Sheriff's Office relating to the arrest of Marcus Satterfield on or about June 8, 2022, on charges including sexual battery, rape, and child molestation.

This request includes, but is not limited to:

1. Initial incident reports and arrest reports, including supplemental and narrative reports
2. Booking records, arrest warrants, and warrant applications
3. Investigative reports, case files, and investigator notes
4. Reports, summaries, or transcripts of interviews with witnesses, complainants, or the arrestee
5. Audio and video recordings of any interviews or interrogations, including forensic interviews
6. 911 calls, dispatch audio, and CAD (computer aided dispatch) logs
7. Photographs and evidence or property logs
8. Emails, memos, or other correspondence about the investigation or arrest

I understand that information identifying any minor or alleged victim may be redacted as required by law. I ask that any such redactions be made so the remainder of each record can be released, rather than withholding records in full.

If any record or portion of a record is withheld, please identify the specific statutory exemption relied on for each, as required by O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71. If you contend that the pending investigation or prosecution exemption in O.C.G.A. § 50-18-72(a)(4) applies, please confirm whether the case is still pending and release the initial arrest and incident reports, which that exemption does not cover.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Silence Dogood

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Signal messages – Aleks Wolan (legislative aide)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

I ask that you acknowledge receipt of this record request once received, and ask for a determination before or on November 30, 2026, per the CPRA, and an even faster reply if you can make that determination without reviewing the record(s) in question.

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act ("CPRA") [Gov't Code §§ 7920.000 et seq.] and the California Constitution [Cal. Const., art. I, § 3(b)(1)], I therefore request the following records in the "possession, control of, relating to, to be about, or to bear on" the City of Berkeley.

RECORDS REQUESTED:

1. Message Threads (Chat History)

All message threads contained on the “Signal” application on the City-issued mobile devices and personal devices of Aleks Wolan, including all messages sent and received, as retained on the application as of November 20, 2026. This includes, for each thread, the complete conversation history from its beginning through the date of this request, with all preceding and subsequent messages preserved in context.

2. Chat-Level Screenshots

For each message thread identified in Item 1, a screenshot of that chat's settings/info screen, showing all information displayed there, including but not limited to:

- whether disappearing messages are enabled (and the timer setting, if so);
- shared media;
- the thread's members/participants; and
- groups in common with other users.

3. Application Settings Screenshots

A screenshot of each of the following settings screens within the Signal application for each employee:

- "Data and Storage"
- "Linked Devices"
- "Backups"
- "Privacy"

4. Home Page Screenshot

A screenshot of the Signal application home page (chat list) for each employee, showing the list of active message threads.

DELIVERY: Please provide records in their original format. For example, email messages in .msg format, including their attachments. Provide text documents on a word-searchable PDF file — capable of Online Text Recognition, and quantitative data in a manipulatable, searchable Excel (XLS) spreadsheet.

As permitted by the CPRA, this Request sets forth the specific categories of information that we are seeking, rather than asking for documents by name [Gov't Code § 7920.530(b)]. It is your obligation to conduct record searches based on the criteria identified herein [see id. §§ 7922.000, 7922.535]. But should you come to believe that the present Request is overly broad, you are required to (1) offer assistance in identifying responsive records and information; (2) describe "the information technology and physical location in which the records exist"; and (3) provide "suggestions for overcoming any practical basis" that you assert as a reason to delay or deny access to the records or information sought [id. § 7922.600(a)].

The CPRA requires that you respond to this Request within ten business days [id. § 7922.535(a)]. No notice shall specify a date that would result in an extension for more than fourteen business days [id. § 7922.535(b)–(c)]. In the written determination, the agency shall state the estimated date when the records will be made available.

If you contend that an express provision of the law exempts a responsive record from disclosure, either in whole or in part, you must make that determination in writing. Such a determination must specify the legal authority on which you rely, as well as identify both the name and title of the person(s) responsible for the determination not to disclose [id. § 7922.000; see also id. § 7922.535(d)].

Additionally, even if you contend that a portion of a record requested is exempt from disclosure, you still must release the non-exempt portion of that record [id. § 7922.525(a), (c)].

Please note that the CPRA "endows" your agency with "discretionary authority to override" any of the Act's statutory exemptions "when a dominating public interest favors disclosure." [CBS, Inc. v. Block, 42 Cal. 3d 646, 652 (1986); see also Nat'l Conference of Black Mayors v. Chico Cmty. Publ'g, Inc., 25 Cal. App. 5th 570, 579 (2018) (construing the CPRA's exemptions as "permissive, not mandatory—they allow nondisclosure but do not prohibit disclosure")]

Because this request pertains to a matter of public concern, I request a fee waiver. None of the information obtained will be sold or distributed for profit. I also request that, to the extent possible, documents be provided in electronic format. Doing so will eliminate the need to copy the materials and provide another basis for the requested fee waiver.

Please copy and send all responsive records as soon as possible, and—if necessary—on a rolling basis to this online records portal. If you have any questions, please email me as soon as possible.

Thank you in advance for your assistance with this request. I look forward to receiving your response within ten business days, by November 30, 2026.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson

title: Barnacle Parking Enforcement invoices and statements (Village Of Chicago Ridge)

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: Barnacle Parking Enforcement invoices and statements (Village Of Chicago Ridge)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I request the following records concerning use of the "Barnacle" windshield immobilizer supplied by ITSA Solutions, LLC d/b/a Barnacle Parking Enforcement ("Barnacle"), for the period January 1, 2026 through June 30, 2026:

1. All invoices from Barnacle, and records of payment on them.
2. All statements, remittance advices, settlement or payout reports, or similar records showing money that Barnacle or its payment processor collected from motorists and paid, credited, or retained for any purpose. This includes records showing fines collected, deposits collected, refunded, or forfeited, surcharges and convenience fees Barnacle kept, and offsets for chargebacks, refunds, or lost or damaged devices.
3. If no record responsive to item 2 exists, a transaction report for the period exported from the Barnacle dashboard or management system.
4. The signed Order or other agreement with Barnacle in effect during the period, with any amendments and pricing schedules.

This request includes records held by any contractor that operates parking enforcement on behalf of Village Of Chicago Ridge. Where records exist as spreadsheets or CSV files, please produce them in that format. If Village Of Chicago Ridge did not use the Barnacle during this period, please say so.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

If you withhold or redact any record, please cite the specific FOIA exemption for each withholding.

Sincerely,

HCvP
